sources.citation: Gordon, Raymond G., Jr. (ed.) 2005. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 15th edition. Dallas: SIL International. Entry 'Bhaya [bhe]' (web version, Wayback capture 2008).
sources.note: Nothing; same content as the 14th edition entry.

sources.citation: Grimes, Barbara F. (ed.) 2000. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 14th edition. Dallas: SIL International. Entry 'BHAYA [BHE]' (web version, Wayback capture 2003).
sources.note: Nothing. Entry gives population 70-700 (1998), Lower Sindh locations (Kapri Goth near Samaro, Khipro, Jamesabad, Mirpurkhas, Phuladia, Hyderabad), a key-morpheme note (possessive postposition in g-, Rajasthani-type gender endings, possible identity with Bhoyari of India) and lexical-similarity percentages from an unpublished 1998 SIL Sindh survey; no phonology.

sources.note: Nothing; confirms the only references are Rahman 2006 (policy overview), Ethnologue, ELCat, World Oral Literature Project; most extensive description = 'wordlist or less'.

sources.citation: SIL International, Sindh sociolinguistic survey (ca. 1994-1998), unpublished field report(s) and wordlists on the minor Indo-Aryan communities of lower Sindh (Bhaya, Goaria, Jandavra, Ghera, Gurgula, Kabutra, Loarki, Vaghri etc.) — the source of the Ethnologue 14 (2000) Bhaya entry.
